results.controlIntent: a. Generate time stamps for audit records using internal system clocks; and b. Record those time stamps for audit records such that the time stamps meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint — CreateEndpoint (2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) and UpdateEndpoint (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z) — carry timestamps that satisfy AU-8.r1 requirements: (a) they are generated by AWS CloudTrail's internal system clocks, which are authoritative and synchronized; and (b) they are recorded in ISO 8601 format with second-level granularity and the 'Z' suffix, explicitly denoting Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This satisfies the UTC requirement under AU-8.r1(b). AWS CloudTrail is a managed service that inherently uses synchronized UTC clocks, so time-source integrity is structurally guaranteed. Confidence is medium rather than high because no organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm that second-level precision meets the stated organizational requirement, and no explicit NTP/time-sync configuration evidence for any custom compute was retrievable.
gaps: No organization-defined granularity policy document available to confirm that second-level timestamp precision meets the stated organizational requirement for AU-8.r1(b).

No NTP or time-synchronization configuration evidence available for any custom compute resources (e.g., training instances, containers) associated with the model — only CloudTrail (a managed AWS service) was assessed.
No evidence of a formal time-source policy or procedure specifying approved time sources for internal system clocks.
